groups.root_cause: After escalation, the engine drops the exclusion for the exhausted implementer, so when the next implementer becomes unavailable, routing falls back to the exhausted one.
Environment-blocked verify retries do not keep the blocked verifier excluded, so the pinned chain picks the same verifier again instead of the available alternative.
The pinned-verify independence warning always names the implementer, even when the excluded model was a previous verifier or a finder.
In panel review mode, a single-entry review chain lets the finders run but leaves no allowed verifier once a finding is raised, so the run stops at needs_human after the finders have been paid for.
Pinned-chain handling throws away a decision model's low-confidence last-resort result instead of accepting it the way policy selection does.
Chain-mode routing ignores vendor independence as a tie-break between `|` alternatives, so it can pick the implementer's vendor and then wrongly log that no other vendor was available.
